title: Chiangmai

endonym.native: เทศบาลนครเชียงใหม่

capsule: Chiang Mai functioned as the capital of the Lanna kingdom until the city and surrounding region fell under Burmese Konbaung suzerainty in 1763, after which it was administered as a semi-autonomous tributary governed by local Chao (princes) of the Chetton dynasty under Burmese overlordship. Kawila, appointed ruler in 1782 with Siamese backing, drove out the Burmese and repopulated the depopulated city, inaugurating a period of gradual reorientation toward Bangkok. By the 1874 Chiang Mai Treaty the region was recognized as a Siamese protectorate, and in 1892 Siam absorbed it into a formal monthon (administrative circle), ending indigenous autonomy; the dataset's terminal date of 1885 reflects the effective consolidation of Siamese administrative control over the princes.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political status of 19th-century Chiang Mai is well documented in Thai, Burmese, and British colonial sources, though the boundary of the tributary zone is imprecisely mapped.
